Play to Learn, Don't play to win

This mindset not only makes you better at the game (because you always keep on learning), it also keeps down your tilt level.
If you don't play to win, but play to learn, a loss isn't just a shitty game gone bad, but a valuable learning experience.

At a more hypothetical level, you can also win more games on a short term.
If you play to learn, you will never surrender (because there's always stuff to learn, especially when you're behind/losing/playing bad). If you won't surrender, there is a chance (hence the hypothetical level) to turn around a losing game and make it a win.

The disadvantage of playing to learn, rather than playing to win, is that LoL is a very competitive game and it can be hard to change your mindset.

I'm pretty much limited to water therapy too as anything I try to do on land tends to result in me doing more harm than good. I love the water therapy though. I have two awesome physiotherapists in the pool with me, and they kit me up with a floating head and neck brace, noodle floats under my armpits/back and under my hips and then these little ring floats that they strap my ankles into to stop my legs sinking.

They basically move my body for me as I can't really do much by myself, even the resistance of the water can be enough for my joints to come apart, although I'm better than I was when I started doing it!

If they take the ankle floats off, I can even kind of stand up now if I'm in the deep end and up to my chin in the water! :D

The therapists stand one either side and trap my legs between their legs to stop my joints buckling. Even with them, the water and the floats supporting me I can't do it for long but it's just so nice to be upright once in a while. I have to be careful though as not only do my legs give way if I do it too long, my heart is too weak to pump the blood back up from my legs so I pass out.

Even in my wheelchair I have to have special footrests that can be adjusted to raise my legs right up. It's awkward as hell driving around with your legs stuck straight out in front of you though!
